items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We never had any job with Hershal which was a pity because I believe that we would have been more inspired playing for dancers than we were at the rehearsals which were quite inspiring with Hershal. Brown at the keyboard.

ctx.x: And in my opinion, Hershal was the second best pianist after Edgar Hayes and he probably would have become considered one of the greats of that era if he had known how to read. He was about the age of Edgar Courance and myself.

We never had any job with Hershal which was a pity because I believe that we would have been more inspired playing for dancers than we were at the rehearsals which were quite inspiring with Hershal. Brown at the keyboard.

Sometime later a fellow came to Cincinnati from Kentucky who's name was Zack White. His name was really Zacharias White and he played banjo. There was also a pianist named Johnny Johnson that I had heard when I was living on Kenyon Avenue. Johnny Johnson also played piano by ear and he was well known in the higher society negro class.
